title: n=2 external-gap candidate: locale-sum (de-DE decimal quirk) — held-out harness, distinct flavor from task-transcript
summary: Built a SECOND external-gap held-out candidate to replicate the n=1 memory-win, deliberately a DIFFERENT flavor (locale-decimal hidden-data, not window-correlation). Task: sumAmounts(rows) totals an upstream billing export's string `amount` field; prose spec shows ONLY en-US amounts. Held-out grader (locale-sum.grader.js, agent never sees it) builds the feed programmatically with 7 non-edge en-US rows + 8 EDGE rows containing de-DE amounts ("1.234,56"=1234.56, "99,90"=99.90). A spec-faithful Number()/parseFloat parser passes 7/7 non-edge but 0/8 edge (Number('1.234,56')=NaN dropped; parseFloat('99,90')=99 truncated). EXTERNALITY: candidate deps:[] so NOTHING but the prose spec enters the worktree — no data file/source to audit; the only cheap path to the edge rows is seeded empirical note note-mq7ydrv353p ("feed mixes en-US and de-DE decimal formats; normalize: if both . and , present the LAST is the decimal, if only , it's the decimal"). Note verified #1 semantic hit at score 0.65 (>0.55 inject threshold) from a natural task query. Reference-impl validation: naive en-US parser 7/15 (0/8 edge), locale-aware parser 15/15 (8/8 edge) — trap well-formed. Registered in scripts/bench-heldout.js. Protocol mirrors task #7: prose-only solve, freeze, post-hoc external grade; rigging guard (3 cold) FIRST, then cold(off) vs warm(on --consult=search) N>=5.
